prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Repaint this exact fountain as worn architectural stone rather than a rendered collectible icon.
Image1 is target: preserve1324x1188 canvas, basin/column/base size, overall footprint and camera. Image2 USER'S ORIGINAL B1 masonry is the primary drawing and palette reference. Image3 actual original character supplies selective ink language.
Change the MATERIAL DRAWING, not just its color. The current basin has a uniformly beveled polygon ring, triangular modeled facets and a glossy patterned water surface: REMOVE those icon conventions. Paint a broad dull hand-cut grey stone rim, with an interrupted dark contour, just TWO large shallow chips and a few quiet uneven stone masses. NO continuous bright top bevel, no shiny edge band. Simplify bowl underside into TWO large ink-black masses connected to the support, instead of repeated equal triangular facets. The shaft and foot are heavy simple blocks with quiet planar shading, like B1 pillars, not an ornamental trophy. Allow some edges to disappear into the dark side shadow. Use actual drawn angular silhouettes with broad solid black shapes; no photographic material grain, tiny cracks, rubble or extra decoration.
Palette: low-chroma NEUTRAL cool grey stone, midplanes aroundRGB75/80/86, highlights100/105/110 maximum except tiny water point. NO yellow, brown, olive or gold. Pool is a single quiet dark slate-grey plane with just one broken subtle ripple; remove the repeated jagged reflective pattern. Thin DIM grey-blue arc from existing spout, no glow, white sparkle or cyan jewel. Do not tint all the stone blue.
This must sit naturally on the B1 floor with matching foreshortening. Keep basin lip camera and original bottom corners. True alpha0 exterior immediately outside painted silhouette, NO ambient haze, aura, halo, shadow cloud or backdrop. Interior ink blacks remain fully opaque. One transparent PNG, no text.
